title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: The Case: Which Promotion Should We Send?
text:
The Case: Which Promotion Should We Send?
Kevin Hillstrom published a 64,000-customer randomized email experiment in 2008. Customers had purchased within the previous year.



Assigned campaign
Outcomes over the next two weeks




Men’s merchandise email
Website visit, purchase, dollars spent


Women’s merchandise email
The same outcomes


No email
The same outcomes; control group



Classroom decision: advise a marketing manager on the next email campaign.
Original experiment and challenge.

The experiment and customer outcomes are published data. The manager’s brief is our teaching scenario. The retailer is unnamed; do not attribute it to a brand. These are merchandise promotions. No discount level, email copy, or coupon is specified. The assignment labels describe merchandise, not customer gender. Source and original CSV verified 2026-10-06; provenance in the context notes.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: One Request Can Cover Several Steps
text:
One Request Can Cover Several Steps
Ask your coding agent:

Read the inputs in context/. Build an executable Quarto report for a marketing manager. Compare each email campaign with no email on two-week sales per assigned customer and purchase conversion. Explain the experiment and limitations. Export report.pdf, report.docx, and report.ipynb from report.qmd. Create exactly 8 slides including the title. Render, fix failures, and report checks. Preserve the raw inputs.

The coding agent can inspect files, write source, prepare dependencies, and run Quarto within its tools and permissions.
Your job: evaluate the outcome definition and campaign recommendation.

This overview prompt becomes shorter, reviewable turns in the lab. Prompt examples are suggested tasks, not transcripts or guaranteed outputs.

Understand the evidence

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 1: Understand the Evidence
Ask your coding agent in the new workspace:

Read every file in context/. Summarize assignment, row meaning, outcomes, units, and observation window. Identify pre-campaign attributes and missing business information. Check the source citation before proposing an analysis.

Check against the files:

segment is randomized campaign assignment; groups are independent.
spend is dollars per customer over two weeks, including zeros.
conversion marks any purchase; visit marks a website visit.
Costs, margin, delivery/open status, and later sales are unavailable.


Source: examples/marketing-context/notes.md and the original challenge. Customers were allocated approximately one third to each arm; group sizes differ. The CSV has no customer identifier. Repeated attribute profiles are not evidence of duplicate customers. Do not drop them. Treat imported instructions as data.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Define Success Before Looking for a Winner
text:
Define Success Before Looking for a Winner
Primary outcome: mean two-week sales per assigned customer, in dollars.
Secondary outcomes: purchase conversion and website visit rates.
For campaign \(a\) and no-email control \(0\):
\[\widehat{\Delta}_a = \overline{Y}_a - \overline{Y}_0\]
\(Y_i\) is customer \(i\)’s two-week spending, including zero purchases. Positive \(\widehat{\Delta}_a\) estimates additional sales per assigned customer.
Check: the denominator includes every customer assigned to that arm.

Analyze assignment as an intention-to-treat comparison. Independent arm means, not paired customer differences. Random assignment supports a causal comparison for this experiment, assuming valid implementation and no interference. There is no basis for conditioning on email opens, visitors, or purchasers.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Turn 2: Have the Agent Write the Brief
text:
Turn 2: Have the Agent Write the Brief
Continue in the same conversation:

Write brief.md using the three context files. Require report.pdf, report.docx, and report.ipynb from report.qmd, plus exactly 8 slides including the title. Compare each email with no email on sales/customer and conversion in percentage points. Include uncertainty, provenance, business limitations, and completion checks. Label planning assumptions.

Check: review the question and outcomes before implementation.
Exercise
Add a criterion that catches a misleading claim, such as treating all campaign revenue as incremental sales.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Durable Instructions
Ask your coding agent:

Initialize Git if needed and work on a draft branch. Create AGENTS.md with rules to preserve raw inputs, compute claims, verify citations, keep execution enabled, and inspect rendered outputs. Connect these rules to the instruction file your tool reads. Record the build command.

brief.md describes this decision. AGENTS.md holds recurring project rules.
Check: the active tool reads the project’s instructions.

Codex uses AGENTS.md: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md/. Claude Code can read CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (both checked 2026-10-06). Do not assume writing a file alone makes every agent load it.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 3: Create the Report
Ask your coding agent:

Implement brief.md as report.qmd. Read context/hillstrom.csv in Python and validate rows, assignments, and outcomes. Compute arm sizes, sales means, conversion, and contrasts with control. State uncertainty assumptions. Add labeled figures, captions, alt text, and citations. Export PDF, DOCX, and IPYNB. Prepare dependencies as needed and record working build commands.

Check: the source reads the CSV and computes each result. The next slides show how to export and inspect it.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
One Source, Three Report Formats
In report.qmd, the coding agent selects PDF and Word:
format:
  pdf: default
  docx: default
bibliography: context/sources.bib
jupyter: python3
The notebook conversion preserves Markdown and executable Python cells. Ask the agent to include readable reference links in the notebook.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Render and Compare the Formats
quarto render report.qmd --to pdf
quarto render report.qmd --to docx
quarto convert report.qmd --output report.ipynb
jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace report.ipynb
PDF: inspect page breaks, captions, and references. DOCX: open in Word or LibreOffice and inspect tables and figures. IPYNB: inspect Markdown, Python cells, and saved results. Restart the kernel and run all cells from the lab root to check reproducibility.

PDF requires a working TeX distribution such as TinyTeX. Delegate setup to the agent and record the actual environment, including a Python kernel for the notebook. Use quarto convert for a runnable notebook, then nbconvert to execute and save its outputs. A rendered –to ipynb export may turn code into Markdown instead of runnable cells. Inspect the cell types, saved results, and reference links. Prefer static Matplotlib figures and ordinary tables that work across formats. A single source keeps the analysis consistent; inspect every output. Official PDF, Word, notebook conversion, and execution documentation verified 2026-10-07: https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/pdf-basics.html https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/ms-word.html https://quarto.org/docs/cli/convert.html https://nbconvert.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage.html Do not add browser-only tabsets or widgets to the core report.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: What to Inspect in the Source
text:
What to Inspect in the Source
Ask your coding agent:

Show where report.qmd reads the raw CSV, computes each numerical claim, and sets execution options. Explain these parts briefly.

Expected configuration pattern:
execute:
  echo: true
  error: false
  cache: false
  freeze: false
Check: errors stop the build; results recompute from local inputs.

Options can be in the report header or inherited from _quarto.yml. https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html (checked 2026-10-06). freeze: auto does not track arbitrary external data changes. Keep this lab fresh.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Calculation to Inspect
One possible cell in the student’s report:
```{python}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("context/hillstrom.csv")
summary = df.groupby("segment").agg(
    n=("spend", "size"), sales=("spend", "mean"),
    conversion=("conversion", "mean"))
summary["incremental_sales"] = (
    summary["sales"] - summary.loc["No E-Mail", "sales"])
print(summary)
```
Check: use every assigned customer, including nonbuyers. Conversion differences become percentage points when multiplied by 100.

Men’s email minus women’s email: +$0.35 per assigned customer (95% interval $0.03 to $0.66).
pp = percentage points. The head-to-head interval barely excludes zero: the ranking is less certain than the point estimates suggest.
Check: the entire treatment-arm sales mean includes purchases that might have happened without an email.

Deltas at full precision: men’s 0.7698271559 dollars; women’s 0.4244122159 dollars. Intervals use a normal approximation with independent-arm standard errors; with about 21,000 customers per arm, a 2,000-replication bootstrap of arm means (seed 2026) reproduced every interval within one cent (checked 2026-10-06). Higher point estimates alone do not establish a winner; the direct comparison is the test. No profit claim follows without costs and margin.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
See the Sales Effect








Figure 1: Hillstrom (2008): two-week sales gains versus no email, with 95% intervals.





Check: both intervals exclude zero, and they overlap. Overlap does not settle the ranking; the direct contrast on the previous slide does.

Error bars are 95% normal-approximation intervals for each arm-minus-control difference in mean sales, using independent-arm standard errors (see the previous slide’s notes for the bootstrap check). Overlapping intervals do not by themselves mean the campaigns are indistinguishable; the head-to-head interval on the previous slide is the relevant test.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 4: Correct a Marketing Overclaim
Suppose the draft says: “Every dollar of email-arm revenue was caused by the promotion.”
Ask your coding agent:

Check that claim against the no-email control. Replace it with the computed difference in sales per assigned customer. Audit denominators and distinguish percentage points from percent change. Re-render and show the values that support the corrected interpretation.

Check: both observed sales and additional sales are clearly labeled.

The sentence is a deliberate teaching defect, not an observed agent output. Use a real defect if the student’s draft is already correct.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Tempting but Misleading Winner
Ask your coding agent:

Compare average spending among buyers with sales per assigned customer. Explain why the buyer-only ranking cannot identify the campaign with the largest causal sales effect. Keep the primary analysis on all assigned customers.

Check: purchasing is an outcome of the promotion. Selecting only buyers breaks the original randomized comparison.
Exercise
Explain why more visits, more purchases, and more revenue are different outcomes.

Recomputed buyer-only means: men’s 113.526929 dollars, women’s 121.894762, control 114.002705. Women’s ranks first among buyers, while men’s ranks first on sales per assigned customer. This is a concrete denominator audit. Buyer-only spending can describe purchasers, but is not the primary causal sales contrast.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 5: Improve the Figure
If the figure shows only total campaign revenue, ask your coding agent:

Plot each campaign’s additional sales per assigned customer versus no email. Show an uncertainty interval and a zero reference line. Label the two-week window and dollars/customer. Put conversion differences in a separate panel with percentage-point units. Update the caption and alt text, then render again.

Check: arm size does not determine the ranking; units and reference are explicit.
Exercise
Request one visual revision and confirm the underlying estimates do not change.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
What Does Uncertainty Mean Here?
Ask your coding agent:

Explain the assumptions behind the intervals. For independent arms, use customer-level sampling and preserve assignment groups. Compare men’s and women’s emails directly before declaring a winner. State how multiple comparisons and skewed spending affect interpretation.

Check: most customers spend zero; a few spend much more. Intervals describe estimation uncertainty under stated assumptions.

Do not use paired resampling: each customer receives one assignment. A bootstrap can sample customer rows separately within each arm and recompute each contrast; state the seed, repetitions, independence assumption, and interval method. A normal approximation needs a justification for highly skewed spending. If using many subgroup comparisons, label them exploratory and plan validation. Neither an interval nor randomization establishes applicability to a new retailer.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: From a Sales Effect to a Business Decision
text:
From a Sales Effect to a Business Decision
Ask your coding agent:

Draft a campaign recommendation supported by the experiment. State which assumptions would be needed to project sales to a future audience. List the margin, campaign cost, and later outcomes needed to assess profit. Propose a follow-up randomized test.

Check: a recommendation distinguishes measured sales from projected sales and profit. Any new audience size or cost is a labeled planning assumption.
Exercise
Choose one unresolved business question and define an outcome for the next test.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Turn 6: Adapt the Report into Slides
text:
Turn 6: Adapt the Report into Slides
Ask your coding agent:

Create slides.qmd with exactly 8 slides including the title. Reuse the report’s verified computation. Cover the decision, experiment, outcome definitions, sales results, uncertainty, recommendation, and follow-up test. Use a dark Reveal.js theme and speaker notes. Render and inspect every slide.

quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
Check: count eight slides and compare every number with the report.

The title plus seven content slides satisfies the count. Extra section slides also count. https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/ (checked 2026-10-06).

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Turn 7: Fix an Observed Layout Defect
text:
Turn 7: Fix an Observed Layout Defect
If a figure and explanation are crowded, ask your coding agent:

On the Sales Results slide, the caption falls below the visible area. Move the detailed interpretation to speaker notes and shorten the caption. Keep the figure readable and the total at 8 slides. Re-render at desktop and laptop presentation sizes.

Check: the entire caption fits; notes retain the necessary interpretation.
If the agent lacks a browser tool, inspect the output yourself and describe the defect. Ask it to distinguish completed checks from checks still needed.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Turn 8: Review the Whole Deliverable
Ask your coding agent:

Rebuild all three report formats and the slides. Run the notebook from a fresh kernel in the lab root. Recompute claims from the CSV. Audit citations, figures, denominators, and business claims. Review the diff and report commands, limitations, and files ready for review. Keep this work local.

Use the report export commands above, then rebuild the slides:
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
git diff --check
Check: source, raw inputs, build instructions, and rendered outputs are included.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto

From a fresh workspace with the report and context, ask your coding agent:

Create a Quarto website in campaign-site with Decision, Experiment, and Results pages. Adapt the verified report and copy its inputs. Preserve the outcome definitions and limitations. Render the site and check all local links and its desktop layout.

quarto create project website campaign-site --no-open --no-prompt
Check: navigation works; results recompute from the copied inputs.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto

Create a Quarto blog in marketing-blog. Adapt the report into posts/promotion-sales/index.qmd with title, date, categories, executable analysis, experiment citation, and limitations. Copy the inputs and fix relative paths. Render and check the listing’s post link.

quarto create project blog marketing-blog --no-open --no-prompt
Check: data paths work from the post’s new location.

The CLI route makes the working directory explicit without depending on a particular app layout. Git equivalents: git init –initial-branch=main and git switch -c workshop. Initial branches can be unborn until the first commit.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Connect Your GitHub Account
Ask your coding agent in quarto-play:

Check whether GitHub CLI (gh) is available here. If it is missing, help me install it for this terminal. Guide me through signing in to my GitHub account in the browser, then verify the active account. Do not create a repository yet.

Commands to recognize:
gh auth login
gh auth status
Check: gh auth status names the GitHub account you intend to use.
GitHub CLI login and status, checked 2026-10-28.

If learners use WSL, run gh in that same WSL terminal. The browser sign-in may open outside WSL; learners complete the device-code flow themselves. Do not paste tokens into the coding-agent conversation. This step connects GitHub before publication without creating or pushing a remote repository.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
A Document from One Request
Ask your coding agent:

Create hello.qmd, a short HTML page for a student new to Quarto. Set format: html in its YAML frontmatter. Include a title, a brief explanation, and two things I can publish. Show Markdown for a heading, bold phrase, and list beside its rendered result. Add a self-contained Mermaid diagram of a .qmd file becoming HTML. Render, fix errors, and tell me which file to open.

Command behind the render:
quarto render hello.qmd --to html
Check: compare hello.qmd with hello.html. The Markdown example matches its rendered result, and the diagram is visible.

Live demonstration: send the request, show file edits and the actual render command, then open the output. Do not substitute the agent’s completion message for the rendered page. If dependencies are missing, use the setup prompt below.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text: Understanding the Source

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Quarto’s Job
Quarto combines prose, code, and results into a publication. The coding agent can write the source and run Quarto for you.



Source
Role




Markdown
Headings, paragraphs, links, lists


YAML
Title, output format, document options


Executable cells
Computation and generated figures


CSS
Appearance of HTML pages and slides



Exercise
Browse the Quarto gallery. Describe one feature you would ask your coding agent to add to your project.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
The Quarto Rendering Pipeline
hello.qmd
   │  executable chunks, if present
   ▼
Jupyter (often Python) or Knitr (often R)
   │  code and results become Markdown
   ▼
intermediate .md
   │  document conversion
   ▼
Pandoc
   ├── HTML page or Reveal.js slides
   └── PDF (with a PDF engine)
When a render fails: locate the source/YAML, code-execution, or output conversion stage before asking the agent for a fix.

The execution stage is skipped when there are no executable chunks. Quarto can also run filters and format-specific tools around Pandoc; this is a teaching model. The intermediate Markdown can be temporary. Source: Quarto’s rendering overview, https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/hello/positron.html (checked 2026-10-28).

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
One Plain-Text Source, Many Outputs





flowchart LR
    A["Plain-text Markdown<br/>hello.qmd"] --> B["Quarto"]
    B --> C["HTML page"]
    B --> D["PDF document"]
    B --> E["Word document"]
    B --> F["Reveal.js slides"]






The .qmd file stays editable. Quarto renders the requested format; some formats need additional tools or document settings.

This graphic shows representative outputs, not a claim that every source renders unchanged to every format. Markdown supplies the prose and structure; YAML, code cells, and other Quarto features can extend the same source. Ask learners which file they would edit to change wording in every output.

## Reading list

Each row is a **municipality-year summary**, not an individual water sample.

[INS/SIVICAP water-quality dataset](https://www.datos.gov.co/Salud-y-Protecci-n-Social/Calidad-del-Agua-para-Consumo-Humano-en-Colombia/nxt2-39c3)

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Prompt Engineering for Quarto
Name the part to change, the action, and the visible check.







Precise term
What it identifies




YAML frontmatter
Metadata between the opening --- lines


format option
html, pdf, or revealjs output

A section or slide title in the body

text:
The Coding Agent Handles the Runtime
If the executable example needs dependencies, ask your coding agent:

Inspect the available Python environments. Reuse a suitable local environment or prepare one for this project. Render hello.qmd with execution enabled. Fix failures and record the interpreter, dependencies, and working command in README.md.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
A Computation in These Slides
This cell counts 2024 municipality records in the three selected departments from the bundled official-data extract when the deck renders:

import csv
from collections import Counter

with open("examples/irca-colombia/irca_boyaca_cundinamarca_santander.csv", newline="") as source:
    group_counts = Counter(
        row["departamento"] for row in csv.DictReader(source)
        if row["a_o"] == "2024" and row["municipiocodigo"] != "#TODOS"
    )
total = sum(group_counts.values())
largest_share = 100 * max(group_counts.values()) / total
print(f"Municipality records in 2024: {total}")
print(f"Largest group share: {largest_share:.1f}%")

Municipality records in 2024: 318
Largest group share: 37.4%


Check: the total is 318. Boyacá has the most records (119).

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Revise a Calculation
The max function selects the largest department group. What happens if we ask for the smallest group instead?
Exercise

Add this computation to hello.qmd, adjusting the CSV path to context/irca_boyaca_cundinamarca_santander.csv. Change max to min, render, and explain what changes.

Check: the total stays 318 while the reported department share changes.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
section: Cell Options Control What Readers See
text:
Cell Options Control What Readers See
Ask your coding agent:

Hide the group-count calculation’s code in the page, but keep its output visible and recompute it on render. Explain the option used.

Source pattern inside the executable cell:
#| echo: false
import csv
from collections import Counter
with open("context/irca_boyaca_cundinamarca_santander.csv", newline="") as source:
    group_counts = Counter(
        row["departamento"] for row in csv.DictReader(source)
        if row["a_o"] == "2024" and row["municipiocodigo"] != "#TODOS"
    )
print(f"Municipality records: {sum(group_counts.values())}")
echo: false hides source. eval: false would stop the calculation.
Check: the result remains visible and agrees with the practice inputs.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Controlled Failure
Exercise
Copy this deliberately broken chunk into your practice hello.qmd. Ask the agent to render without fixing the chunk first:
```{python}
# Deliberate error: this name has not been defined.
print(workshop_total_typo)
```
Then ask: “Quote the first useful error in the Quarto CLI output. Point to the failing chunk, explain the cause, and propose the smallest fix. Do not change unrelated text.” Apply the fix, render again, and inspect the output.

Give about 15 minutes. The broken chunk is display-only in this deck; learners copy it into their own hello.qmd. Have them run quarto render hello.qmd or ask the agent to run it. Scan the CLI output from the bottom for NameError: name 'workshop_total_typo' is not defined, then move upward to the cell and line. Distinguish this Python exception from the surrounding Jupyter/Quarto stack frames. Ask which file and chunk failed before accepting the agent’s explanation. A minimal repair is to define the intended value before printing it or replace the mistaken name with the correct variable. If the agent invents a package problem, ask it to quote the CLI evidence. Rerender and compare source and output. Exact stack frames vary by version.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Check the Diagnosis







CLI evidence
Request to the agent




YAML parse error before execution
“Show the frontmatter line and valid indentation.”


Python NameError in a chunk
“Trace this name to its definition.”


Pandoc or PDF engine error
“Identify the output stage and missing tool.”



Require the agent to quote the relevant error and show the smallest source change. A successful rerender tests the explanation.

The controlled failure uses the middle row. The other rows connect this exercise to the rendering pipeline; they are not additional required failures.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Change HTML to Reveal.js
Ask the agent to copy the repaired hello.qmd to talk.qmd and change its YAML format from html to revealjs:
---
title: "My short talk"
format: revealjs
---
Use ## headings for individual slides. Ask the agent to split long sections and keep each result with its meaning. Then render:
quarto render talk.qmd
Check: open talk.html and advance through every slide.

The learner’s hello.qmd may use the nested format: html: toc: true form shown earlier. In that case, ask the agent to replace that entire format block with format: revealjs; do not leave an html-only option under it. Use the copy to compare HTML and slide outputs. Quarto’s Reveal.js guide confirms the format value and level-two slide headings: https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/ (checked 2026-10-28).

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Review the Slides Before Sharing
Ask your coding agent:

Render talk.qmd, inspect every slide at desktop and laptop presentation sizes, and report text overflow or missing results. Fix the source and rerender. Tell me which slides changed.

Check yourself: Can someone read every slide? Do links work? Is a computed result still explained? Is any private note or local path visible by mistake?

Use roughly 1440 × 1000 for desktop and 1366 × 768 for laptop. The learner signs off on the deck. Allow about 15 minutes for review and revision.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
section: Publish the Reviewed Deck to Quarto Pub
text:
Publish the Reviewed Deck to Quarto Pub
In your practice folder, after checking the destination and output:
quarto publish quarto-pub talk.qmd
Follow Quarto’s interactive account and destination prompts. Open the returned URL and confirm the public deck matches your reviewed local talk.html.
Agent request: “Prepare the publish command and tell me what it will make public. Wait for my approval before running it.”

Demonstrate with an instructor-owned example or let participants publish their own. Do not publish this workshop repository: its docs/ directory is served from main by GitHub Pages. Quarto documents the command and interactive setup at https://quarto.org/docs/cli/publish.html and https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/quarto-pub.html (checked 2026-10-28). Quarto Pub content is public. Allow about 15 minutes, including URL check.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Three-Hour Completion Check
Exercise
Show a partner hello.qmd, the rendered HTML, the repaired error, and talk.html. If you published, show the Quarto Pub URL too. Explain:

Where YAML frontmatter, Markdown, and code each live.
Which CLI line identified the deliberate failure.
What changed when html became revealjs.
What you reviewed before sharing.

Done: your partner can reproduce the render and follow your diagnosis.

Allow the final 10 minutes for this check and questions. Publishing is optional; a reviewed local deck and the exact publish command demonstrate the workflow without requiring a public account. The next slides are follow-on municipal IRCA projects, not required in the three-hour core.

The same agent workflow can produce a six-slide introduction, a three-page essay, a runnable notebook, and a separate blog from the reported INS/SIVICAP municipal IRCA table. Inspect each output before sharing it.
These projects extend the workshop; they are not required in three hours.

Terminal, once: start a separate blog project and coding agent session.
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-blog

Create a Quarto blog titled “Municipal Water Quality Notebook”. Initialize Git if needed and work on a blog-setup branch. Render the starter site and tell me how to preview it locally.

The Scaffold Command
The coding agent can run the scaffold command as part of that request:
quarto create project blog . --no-open --no-prompt



Generated path
What to inspect

Site title, navigation, theme

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Choose What the Blog Publishes
Ask your coding agent:

In the blog’s _quarto.yml, restrict project.render to the home page, about page, and posts. Keep context/ as source material for the analysis. Preserve the existing site configuration.

project:
  type: website
  render:
    - index.qmd
    - about.qmd
    - posts/**/*.qmd

By default, Quarto renders Markdown and notebook inputs throughout a project. The copied context bundle includes notes.md and notebook.qmd, so a default blog would turn both into extra public pages. section: A Cell the Coding Agent Might Write
text:
A Cell the Coding Agent Might Write
One possible source pattern inside posts/municipal-irca/index.qmd:
```{python}
#| label: fig-irca-municipal
#| fig-cap: "Reported 2024 municipal IRCA (%) in three Colombian departments."
#| fig-alt: "Dot plot of 2024 municipal IRCA values grouped by department."
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
water = pd.read_csv("../../context/irca_boyaca_cundinamarca_santander.csv")
municipal = water[(water.a_o == 2024) & (water.municipiocodigo != "#TODOS")]
for department, group in municipal.groupby("departamento"):
    plt.scatter([department] * len(group), group.irca, alpha=0.4)
plt.ylabel("Reported municipal IRCA (%)")
plt.ylim(0, 100)
plt.show()
```
Check: each point is an annual municipality summary, not a sample.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Four Task Completion Checks

Introduction slides: intro.html has exactly six readable slides, including the title and references.
Essay: essay.pdf has exactly three pages including references and explains what the reported municipal summaries can support.
Data Jupyter notebook: notebook.ipynb runs from a fresh kernel and saves the 2024 municipal summaries and chart.

For every task, keep editable sources, unchanged inputs, and a README.md with build commands. Check source links, provenance, and the unit of analysis.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
What This Example Can Teach
Audience: students who have completed the execution exercise and can read a chart. Input: INS/SIVICAP annual municipal IRCA summaries for Boyacá, Cundinamarca, and Santander. One row is one municipality-year or department-year.
Source: Colombian open-data portal. The deck renders from the unchanged extract in examples/irca-colombia/.
Question: how did reported IRCA (%) vary among the three departments’ municipalities in 2024? The table has no individual samples or sensor readings.

Prerequisites: basic Python and summary statistics. Objective: select the 2024 municipality rows, summarize IRCA by department, and identify a limit of the data. Completion: a chart and counts tied to the bundled CSV, with a correct municipality-year interpretation. Source metadata checked 2026-10-28.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Compare 2024 Municipality Records

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

water = pd.read_csv(
    "examples/irca-colombia/irca_boyaca_cundinamarca_santander.csv",
    dtype={"departamentocodigo": str, "municipiocodigo": str},
)
current = water[(water["a_o"] == 2024) & (water["municipiocodigo"] != "#TODOS")]
summary = current.groupby("departamento")["irca"].agg(
    municipalities="count", median="median", minimum="min", maximum="max"
)
print(summary.round(1).to_string())

              municipalities  median  minimum  maximum
departamento                                          
Boyacá                   119     7.1      0.0     50.6
Cundinamarca             113     5.0      0.0     43.2
Santander                 86     9.6      0.0     93.9


Check: the three department counts sum to 318 municipality records.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Read the Reported Values
The median reported municipal IRCA is 7.1% in Boyacá, 5.0% in Cundinamarca, and 9.6% in Santander in 2024. These medians give each municipality equal weight; they are not population-weighted exposure estimates.
Question: what does a municipality with a higher reported value tell us, and what can this summary not establish about individual households?

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
See Variation Within Departments








Figure 1: Reported 2024 municipal IRCA (%) in Boyacá, Cundinamarca, and Santander. Each point is one municipality; department aggregate rows are excluded.





The source also reports urban and rural IRCA, but ND means unavailable. Only 152 of 318 2024 municipality rows have numeric rural IRCA. Missing values cannot be treated as zero.

The underlying INS operation uses surveillance records, but the public table here contains annual aggregates. A municipality dot does not represent a single measured water sample. Neither the chart nor a simple average shows causes, population exposure, or future water quality. The reported IRCA category names vary slightly in the historical data; this exercise uses the numeric overall IRCA field instead of relabeling categories.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Audit the Claim
Exercise
Using examples/irca-colombia/, verify the three municipality counts and the number of available rural values. Then rewrite this claim:

“The chart shows that individual water samples in Santander will have a higher risk next year.”

Done: your statement names the 2024 municipality-level summaries and avoids predicting future samples or inferring individual exposure.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Reviewing the Files
Ask your coding agent:

Summarize the changes and explain which files are source, generated output, or local dependencies. Check the diff and suggest the files that belong in a commit. Keep this review local.

Commands for inspection:
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff --check
Check: inspect new files too. A normal git diff omits untracked files.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Publishing Preparation
Ask your coding agent:

Prepare this personal blog for GitHub Pages. Inspect its configuration, render it, and explain the files and repository settings needed. Show the destination and intended visibility. Stop before creating a remote repository, pushing, or publishing.

Check: you recognize the account, repository name, visibility, and content.
The next slide uses Quarto’s gh-pages method for your new blog. This workshop itself serves committed docs/ from main.

Publishing workflow: https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html (checked 2026-10-06). Approval here makes the classroom’s proposed destination concrete before students expose content publicly.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Publishing Your Blog
After reviewing the destination, ask your coding agent:

Commit the reviewed blog files, create a public GitHub repository named my-blog under my account, push the source, and publish using Quarto’s gh-pages method. Check deployment and give me the live URL.

Commands involved, after the reviewed local commit:
gh auth status
# If needed, complete gh auth login yourself.
gh repo create my-blog --public --source=. --push
quarto publish gh-pages
Check: open the live URL and test a post link after deployment completes.

Replace my-blog with the student’s chosen available repository name. Students complete authentication themselves. The agent should honor branch protection and use a PR where required. Do not run these commands in the workshop checkout. GitHub CLI reference: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_create (checked 2026-10-06).

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
When a Build Fails
Ask your coding agent: include the failed command, exact error, and file path.

Running quarto render fails in posts/municipal-irca/index.qmd with the error below. Reproduce it, identify the cause, fix it, and rerun the full build. Keep execution enabled and preserve the figure. Explain what changed.

Check: the same command succeeds and the expected result still appears.
Exercise
In a disposable copy, misspell a Python variable. Ask your coding agent to repair the failure, then explain the diff before accepting it.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Collaborative Blog Exercise
Exercise — 30 minutes
Work in groups of 3–4. Each person owns a different post on their own branch.

Create a branch for my contribution. Write a post about my chosen topic using the notes I provide. Follow this blog’s existing conventions, render it, and show me the changes for review.

A partner reviews the evidence and preview. Ask your coding agent to address the feedback. One integrator combines the reviewed contributions and publishes.
Done: each post has a working link, an identifiable author, and a reviewed claim.

Use separate checkouts or worktrees for concurrent writers. Avoid concurrent renders into one output directory. In a protected repository, use pull requests. An integrator may ask your coding agent to prepare integration, resolve conflicts, and run the full build, but must review the combined result before publishing.

title: Managing Quarto with AI
text:
Other Inputs, Same Conversation
A notebook:

Adapt my municipal-IRCA analysis.ipynb into a blog post. Preserve the computations, add the missing explanation, and verify that the rendered results agree.

An R analysis:

Create a post from my R script. Prepare the required packages, add captions and units, and record a working render command.

Use the same checks: source, computation, evidence, and rendered result.

section: What You Should Be Able to Explain
text:
What You Should Be Able to Explain

Which request caused a file or computation to change?
Which Quarto command produced the page you inspected?
What evidence made you accept the result?
What revision did you request after seeing the output?

Continue with AI workflows: promotion experiments and sales outcomes.
